title: IAEA Urges Kenya To Finalise Policies On Radioactive Waste Management
summary: Kenya should finalise national policies on radioactive waste management and strengthen regulatory independence as it prepares to introduce nuclear power, an International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) review mission has said. The IAEA said an international team had recognised “considerable progress” in the east African nation’s radioactive waste management programme in recent years, but identified areas requiring further development.

title: South Korea’s KHNP Breaks Off Construction Contract Talks On Dukovany Reactor Project
summary: Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power (KHNP) has broken off construction contract talks with a Daewoo Engineering & Construction-led consortium for a $18.6bn (€16.5bn) project to build two new nuclear plants at the Dukovany site in the Czech Republic. The state-run nuclear operator said on Thursday (29 October) it would move to terminate its cooperation agreement with the consortium, which includes Doosan Enerbility, and launch a new bidding process to find a replacement contractor. Reports in South Korea said the breakdown followed more than a year of talks over construction costs and who should bear the financial burden of design changes. According to industry sources, KHNP demanded a cut of more than 10% from the consortium’s original bid, equivalent to over $750m.

title: DOE’s ARPA-E selects eight transuranic fuel development projects
summary: The Department of Energy’s Advanced Research Projects Agency–Energy (ARPA-E) division has chosen eight research projects to receive funding as part of its High-Performance Optimized Recycled Nuclear Isotopes for Gen IV Reactors (HORNIG) program. The program, announced in April, seeks to advance Executive Order 14302, “Reinvigorating the Nuclear Industrial Base,” by supporting projects that will develop fuel technology for advanced nuclear reactors. The projects selected for HORNIG will explore ways to repurpose materials from used nuclear fuel inventories—specifically the transuranic waste elements derived from nuclear weapons production, including plutonium—in the domestic production of fuel for commercial reactors.

title: Russia Begins Fuel Deliveries For First Load At Rooppur-2 Nuclear Plant
summary: Russia’s state-owned nuclear corporation Rosatom has begun delivering nuclear fuel for the initial loading of Unit 2 at Bangladesh’s Rooppur nuclear power station, a statement said. Rosatom said that it had completed a first shipment of fuel assemblies manufactured by its Novosibirsk Chemical Concentrates Plant in Russia. The fuel was transported to Bangladesh on a dedicated cargo flight. The company said the fuel containers had been transferred to a storage facility at Rooppur, where the assemblies undergo visual and technical inspections before they can be loaded into the reactor.
